properties.description:
The following message is transmitted in collaboration with the
Wyoming Department of Environmental Quality, Air Quality Division,
and the Wyoming Department of Health.

* WHAT...Air Quality Alert for Wildfire Smoke.

* WHERE...Northeast Wyoming.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Poor air quality due to wildfire smoke.
properties.instruction:
The Wyoming Department of Health recommends the elderly, young
children, and individuals with respiratory problems avoid excessive
physical exertion and minimize outdoor activities during this time.
Wildfire smoke is made up of a variety of pollutants, including
particulate matter and ozone, which can cause respiratory health
effect. Although these people are most susceptible to health
impacts, the Department of Health also advises that everyone should
avoid prolonged exposure to poor air quality conditions.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued August 3 at 11:50AM EDT until August 3 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and strong longshore currents in
the surf zone.

* WHERE...For Rip Currents, the beaches from Cape Hatteras to
Oregon Inlet. For Longshore Currents, the beaches from Oregon
Inlet to Surf City.

* WHEN...From this morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Strong longshore currents will
create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 5:15 PM Monday.
properties.instruction:
Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

properties.instruction:

either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute to
extreme fire behavior.

An Air Quality Alert means that particulates have been trending
upwards and that an exceedance of the 24 hour National Ambient Air
Quality Standard (NAAQS) has occurred or may occur in the near
future.

Elevated particulate levels from wildfire smoke

Falls, Frenchtown, Lewistown, Libby, Missoula and Thompson Falls are
Unhealthy.

for Sensitive Groups.

Hamilton, Helena, Malta and Sleeping Giant are Moderate.

When air quality is Unhealthy... State and local health officials
recommend that people with respiratory or heart disease, the elderly,
and children should avoid prolonged exertion; everyone else should
limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups... State and local
health officials recommend that people with respiratory or heart
disease, the elderly and children should limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Moderate... State and local health officials
recommend that unusually sensitive people should consider reducing
prolonged or heavy exertion.

Quality at http://todaysair.mtdeq.us

river will then continue to fall to 12.8 feet Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

properties.description:
FFWOKX

The National Weather Service in Upton has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Middlesex County in southern Connecticut...
Southeastern New Haven County in southern Connecticut...
New London County in southern Connecticut...

* Until 100 PM EDT.

* At 957 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy downpours and
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen over the last 6 hours.
Rainfall rate of 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour are likely. Additional
rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the warned area
through 1pm. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as
other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Jewett City, Middletown, Norwich, New London, Guilford,
Colchester, Clinton, East Hampton, Groton, Old Saybrook, Durham,
Salem, Chester, Mystic, Branford, Waterford, East Lyme, Ledyard,
North Branford and Griswold.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 3 at 5:08AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
A storm moving in from the Bering Sea will bring widespread,
prolonged rainfall to Southwest Alaska through Tuesday.

- Rain amounts: Through Tuesday afternoon, widespread rainfall
amounts of an additional 1 to 2 inches are expected across
Southwest Alaska, with locally higher amounts possible (up to 3
inches for the Western Alaska Range).

- Timing of heaviest rain: For Kuskokwim Delta and Bristol Bay,
this morning. For Alaska Peninsula and Southwest interior (Lake
Iliamna region and along the Western Alaska Range), Monday into
Tuesday.

- Winds and water levels: For coastal areas from west of
Dillingham to the Western Capes (including the communities of
Togiak, Goodnews Bay, and Platinum), southerly sustained winds
of 25 to 35 mph will persist through Monday afternoon. This
could bring water levels up to 1 foot above the mean high tide
line. Winds will be strongest early Monday morning.

Preparedness: Check the forecast for the latest updates, especially
if you plan to be outdoors or traveling. Along Bristol Bay, beware
of gusty winds and high water levels along the coast.

properties.areaDesc: Western Rogue Basin including the Illinois Valley; Siskiyou Mountains; Eastern Rogue Valley; Southern Oregon Cascades
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued August 3 at 5:04AM PDT until August 4 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Oregon, Fire Weather zones 620, 621, 622,
and 623, including Medford, Grants Pass, Ashland, Cave
Junction, Eagle Point, Shady Cove, and the Siskiyous and
southern Oregon Cascades.

* WIND...Northwest 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph in the
afternoons, becoming east to northeast overnight.

* HUMIDITY...Minimum humidity 8 to 15 percent, with poor
recoveries as low as 20 percent.

* ADDITIONAL INFORMATION...Critical fire weather conditions will
be more prevalent in low-lying areas in the afternoon and
evening due to elevated breezes and minimum RHs. Overnight and
into early morning hours, area peaks and ridgelines will have
critical conditions due to easterly flow and poor recoveries.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Follow all fire restrictions. You can find your county's
emergency sign up form as well as links to fire restrictions at
weather.gov/medford/wildfire. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Be sure you're signed up for your county's emergency alert
system. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan and make
sure you listen to emergency services. Visit ready.gov/plan for
more information.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions
that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-
threatening. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions
are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to
have multiple ways to receive information from authorities.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 3 at 5:10AM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.

WHERE...Moffat, Rio Blanco, Routt, Jackson, Grand, Larimer and
Boulder Counties. Locations include, but are not limited to Craig,
Meeker, Rangely, Steamboat Springs, Walden, Granby, Hot Sulphur
Springs, Kremmling, Fort Collins and Boulder.

WHEN...500 AM Monday August 03 to 900 AM Tuesday August 04

IMPACTS...Areas of moderate to heavy smoke from out-of-state
wildfires will be possible within the advisory area through at
least Tuesday morning.

HEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: Increasing
likelihood of respiratory symptoms in sensitive individuals,
aggravation of heart or lung disease and premature mortality in
people with cardiopulmonary disease and older adults. People with
heart or lung disease, older adults, and children should reduce
prolonged or heavy exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Cuyama Valley
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 3 at 2:45AM PDT until August 4 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot daytime conditions with high temperatures between 95 and
105 common.

* WHERE...The Cuyama Valley.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 8 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for dangerous heat illness,
especially for sensitive groups like the very young, the very old,
those without air conditioning, and those active outdoors.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Heat hazards may extend into next week for
portions of the region.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

If you do not have air conditioning in your home or lack shelter, you
can call 211 for assistance locating appropriate shelter from the
heat.

early Wednesday, especially near heavier showers as a westerly
monsoon surge continues. Additionally, distant Typhoon Dolphin

is moving through the Marianas, which will continue shift north
over the next day or so, then northwest. Meanwhile, the

for much of this week.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot and humid conditions. Afternoon temperatures
107 to 117. Major to Extreme Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Yuma, La Paz, and Eastern Riverside Counties, including the
Colorado River Valley.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST /8 PM PDT/ Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Increase in heat related illnesses, including heat
cramps, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke. Heat stroke can lead to
death.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6

Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Kings (Brooklyn), Southwest Suffolk, Southeast
Suffolk, Southern Queens and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM this morning to 9
PM EDT this evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM
EDT this morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Life-threatening rip currents are
likely for all people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting
the beaches should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can
sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest surf along the ocean beaches of Suffolk
County. Moderate to high rip current expected on Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

If you enter the surf zone, always have a flotation device with
you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued August 3 at 3:56PM ChST until August 8 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:

currents expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...North and east facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM ChST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Long-period east to northeast swell,
emanating from distant Typhoon Dolphin, continues to produce a
high risk of rip currents and hazardous surf along north and
east-facing reefs. As Dolphin continues to move toward Iwo To,
the long-period swell direction is expected to shift north over
the next few days, and then northwest around midweek. As it does
so, a high risk of rip currents and hazardous surf are expected
to develop along west facing reefs later this week.
properties.instruction:

dangerous surf conditions.

the current. If able, swim in a direction following the
shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave
for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 2 at 8:59PM MST until August 3 at 10:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south-central Arizona, including Santa Cruz,
southwest Cochise and south-central and southeast Pima counties.

* WHEN...From 2 pm MST Monday afternoon through 10 pm MST Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall runoff may result in flash flooding of
normally dry washes, roadway dips and other low-lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The combination of an increase in lower-level moisture and an
favorable weather pattern will result in widespread strong
thunderstorms with heavy rain across portions of south- central
Arizona. Although thunderstorms will initially develop over the
higher terrain during the early afternoon, coverage is expected
to become more widespread in the late afternoon and evening
hours. Although most areas impacted by thunderstorms will receive
only between one half to one inch of rain, isolated locations may
receive between 1 and 3 inches. Excessive rainfall runoff will
result in flash flooding.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Blowing Dust Advisory issued August 2 at 8:59PM MST until August 3 at 10:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Thunderstorms will initially develop over the Mogollon Rim
and other sky islands of Southeast Arizona during the early
afternoon, track southwest into the valleys of Southeast Arizona
and become widespread during the late afternoon, then move across
the lower deserts of Southeast Arizona through the evening. The
stronger storms will produce organized thunderstorm outflow winds
between 45-55 mph, resulting in dense blowing dust with visibility
between one-quarter and one-half mile and possibly a haboob with
near-zero visibility. For the Extreme Heat Warning, dangerously hot
conditions with temperatures 107 to 112. Major to Extreme HeatRisk
is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Pinal County, Southeast Pinal County, Tohono
O'odham Nation, and Western Pima County.

* WHEN...For the Extreme Heat Warning, until 8 PM MST Monday. For the
Blowing Dust Advisory, from 4 PM to 10 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to reduced visibility.
Heat related illnesses increase significantly during extreme heat
events.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Warm overnight low temperatures of 84 to 90
degrees in the deserts will provide little to no relief from heat
overnight. Warmest overnight low temperatures expected in the
Western Deserts.
properties.instruction:
Persons with respiratory problems should make preparations to stay
indoors until the storm passes. Be ready for a sudden drop in
visibility to near zero. If you encounter blowing dust or blowing
sand on the roadway or see it approaching, pull off the road as far
as possible and put your vehicle in park. Turn the lights all the way
off and keep foot off the brake pedal. Remember, 'Pull Aside, Stay
Alive'.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

Idaho Department of Environmental Quality in Coeur d'Alene

...AIR QUALITY ADVISORY FROM THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY FOR Boundary, Bonner, Benewah, Kootenai, and Shoshone
Counties...

* WHERE...Boundary, Bonner, Benewah, Kootenai, and Shoshone Counties...

* WHEN...Next update 11 AM PDT August 3rd.

* IMPACTS...Some members of the general public may experience health
effects; members of sensitive groups may experience more serious
health effects.
properties.instruction:

elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
activity during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air
quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

properties.areaDesc: Asotin, WA; Chelan, WA; Douglas, WA; Ferry, WA; Grant, WA; Lincoln, WA; Okanogan, WA; Pend Oreille, WA; Spokane, WA; Stevens, WA
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 2 at 5:42PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
An Air Quality Alert has been issued by the following agencies:

Washington Department of Ecology
Colville Confederated Tribes
Environmental Protection Agency
Spokane Regional Clean Air Agency

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Asotin, Chelan, Douglas,
Ferry, Okanogan, Pend Oreille, and Stevens Counties until further
notice due to current and expected wildfire smoke from regional
fires. Extremely critical fire weather Saturday will produce
significant smoke from ongoing and emerging fires. Particulate matter
(PM2.5) may reach unhealthy levels through the weekend, especially in
areas downwind from active wildfires in Washington, Oregon, and
British Columbia.

An Air Quality Alert has also been issued for Grant, Lincoln, and
Spokane counties until further notice due to expected smoke impacts
from ongoing and emerging fires. Shifting winds will likely bring
smoke into these counties beginning Saturday evening. PM2.5 may reach
unhealthy levels.

When air quality is unhealthy, everyone should reduce exposure.
Limit time outside, avoid strenuous outdoor activity, and follow tips
for cleaner indoor air.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Noatak Valley; Kivalina and Red Dog Dock; Lower Kobuk Valley; Baldwin Peninsula; Northern Seward Peninsula; Shishmaref; Bering Strait Coast; Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Interior Seward Peninsula; Eastern Norton Sound and Nulato Hills; St Lawrence Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 2 at 2:08PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
As a coastal system moves across Western Alaska Sunday into
Monday, elevated water levels, widespread moderate to heavy rain,
and southerly winds are expected across the area. Water levels
could rise 1 to 3 feet above the mean high tide line in coastal
areas of the Bering and Chukchi Seas. Rain totals from Sunday
afternoon through early Tuesday morning are expected to range from
1 to 2 inches south of the Bering Strait and from 0.5 to 1 inch
north of the Bering Strait. From Sunday afternoon through Tuesday
night, southerly winds will gust to 30 to 40 mph. Those in coastal
areas should take extra precautions to ensure that belongings are
properly secured ahead of these increasing winds and water
levels.

NWSheadline: Elevated Water Levels, Widespread Rain, and Wind to Start the Week

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 2 at 2:08PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
As a coastal system moves across Western Alaska Sunday into
Monday, it will bring widespread moderate to heavy rain and
southerly winds across the area. Rain totals from Sunday afternoon
through early Tuesday morning are expected to range from 1 to 2
inches across most of the Western Interior. River levels will rise
with this rainfall, although no flooding is expected. From Sunday
afternoon through Tuesday night, southerly winds could gust as
high as 40 mph in the Lower Yukon and Upper Kuskokwim Valleys,
with gusts over 30 mph possible elsewhere.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 2 at 3:31PM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
properties.description:
AQAFWD

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued
an Ozone Action Day for the Dallas-Fort Worth area for Monday,
August 3, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone air pollution in the Dallas-Fort Worth area
on Monday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by sharing a
ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive-through lanes, conserving energy, and keeping your
vehicle properly tuned.

For more information on ozone:

Ozone: The Facts (www.tceq.texas.gov/goto/ozonefacts)

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 2 at 3:28PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
AQAHGX

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued an
Ozone Action Day for the Houston, Galveston, and Brazoria area for
Monday, August 3, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone pollution in the Houston, Galveston, and
surrounding areas on Monday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by
sharing a ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive through lanes, conserving energy and keeping your vehicle
properly tuned.

For more information on ozone:

properties.areaDesc: Asotin, WA; Chelan, WA; Douglas, WA; Ferry, WA; Grant, WA; Lincoln, WA; Okanogan, WA; Pend Oreille, WA; Spokane, WA; Stevens, WA
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 2 at 12:39PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
An Air Quality Alert has been issued by the following agencies:

Washington Department of Ecology
Colville Confederated Tribes
Environmental Protection Agency
Spokane Regional Clean Air Agency

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Asotin, Chelan, Douglas,
Ferry, Okanogan, Pend Oreille, and Stevens Counties until further
notice due to current and expected wildfire smoke from regional
fires. Extremely critical fire weather Saturday will produce
significant smoke from ongoing and emerging fires. Particulate matter
(PM2.5) may reach unhealthy levels through the weekend, especially in
areas downwind from active wildfires in Washington, Oregon, and
British Columbia.

An Air Quality Alert has also been issued for Grant, Lincoln, and
Spokane counties until further notice due to expected smoke impacts
from ongoing and emerging fires. Shifting winds will likely bring
smoke into these counties beginning Saturday evening. PM2.5 may reach
unhealthy levels.

When air quality is unhealthy, everyone should reduce exposure.
Limit time outside, avoid strenuous outdoor activity, and follow tips
for cleaner indoor air.

properties.areaDesc: Eastern Sierra Slopes of Inyo County; White Mountains of Inyo County; Sheep Range; Spring Mountains-Red Rock Canyon
properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued August 2 at 12:24PM PDT until August 5 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions expected with highs 80 to 90 degrees above
8000 feet and 90 to 100 degrees below 8000 feet. This will result
in Moderate Heat Risk.

* WHERE...In California, Eastern Sierra Slopes and White Mountains of
Inyo County. In Nevada, Sheep Range and Spring Mountains-Red Rock
Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

NWSheadline: HEAT ADVISORY NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM PDT WEDNESDAY

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 2 at 8:24AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air
Quality Advisory for eastern Clackamas County, which is IN EFFECT
UNTIL NOON PDT MONDAY.

An Air Quality Advisory for Smoke has been issued. Wildfires burning
in the region combined with forecasted conditions will cause air
quality to reach unhealthy levels at times through noon PDT Monday.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems. Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

More information about air quality can be found at:
www.oregon.gov/DEQ

properties.description:

Advisory until 2 PM PDT Monday.

For the Smoke Air Quality Advisory, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

For additional information...please visit the Web site at
http://www.oregon.gov/DEQ

Counties.

* WHEN...UNTIL 2 PM MDT MONDAY.

* IMPACTS...Members of sensitive groups may experience health

individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or

limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

properties.areaDesc: Asotin, WA; Chelan, WA; Douglas, WA; Ferry, WA; Grant, WA; Lincoln, WA; Okanogan, WA; Pend Oreille, WA; Spokane, WA; Stevens, WA
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 31 at 12:29PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
An Air Quality Alert has been issued by the following agencies:

Washington Department of Ecology
Colville Confederated Tribes
Environmental Protection Agency
Spokane Regional Clean Air Agency

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Asotin, Chelan, Douglas,
Ferry, Okanogan, Pend Oreille, and Stevens Counties until further
notice due to current and expected wildfire smoke from regional
fires. Extremely critical fire weather Saturday will produce
significant smoke from ongoing and emerging fires. Particulate matter
(PM2.5) may reach unhealthy levels through the weekend, especially in
areas downwind from active wildfires in Washington, Oregon, and
British Columbia.

An Air Quality Alert has also been issued for Grant, Lincoln, and
Spokane counties until further notice due to expected smoke impacts
from ongoing and emerging fires. Shifting winds will likely bring
smoke into these counties beginning Saturday evening. PM2.5 may reach
unhealthy levels.

When air quality is unhealthy, everyone should reduce exposure.
Limit time outside, avoid strenuous outdoor activity, and follow tips
for cleaner indoor air.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

medical conditions. People most at risk to adverse health effects
include infants, young children, people with heart or lung
disease, older adults, and pregnant women.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Smoke levels can change rapidly depending on
weather. Check current conditions on the Oregon Smoke Information
Blog, DEQ's Air Quality Index, or by downloading the free
OregonAIR app on your smartphone.
properties.instruction:
* Stay inside if possible. Keep windows and doors closed.

* Avoid strenuous outdoor activity.

* Use high efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filters in indoor
ventilation systems or portable air purifiers.

* Be aware of smoke in your area and avoid places with the highest
levels.

* If you have heart or lung disease, or asthma, follow your
healthcare provider's advice.

For current Oregon air quality conditions, please visit:
https://aqi.oregon.gov

For additional information, please visit:
https://www.oregon.gov/deq
